key_insights.algebraic_step_proved: nf_eval_from_lower_agree inductive step (d >= 1, n >= 1) is sorry-free. Uses exist_transfer_from_full_agree for depth-d matched witnesses, nf_agreement_from_shared_nf for full agreement, IH for depth upgrade. This is the CORE algebraic mechanism.
key_insights.counterexample_for_base: M = (Q, <) with P only at z=1, env=[0,2]. N = (Q, <) with P at -1 and 5, env=[0,2]. Both Prior structures. h_1var at depth 1 matches (chi with P(y)>0 true in both; chi with P(y)<2 true in both). But ∃ z' in (0,2) with P in N fails (P only at -1 and 5). Additional check: h_1var at x=2 fails because ∃ y>2 with P is false in M but true in N (y=5). So counterexample requires P constrained to interval by h_1var.
key_insights.partial_resolution: For the specific application (r=2, env=[x,t]), h_1var constraints DO force P into [t',x']: no P below t' (from h_1var at t), no P above x' (from h_1var at x), P(t')=false and P(x')=false (from pred agreement). Combined with P existing above t' and below x': P must exist in (t',x'). This argument is specific to r=2 and uses properties of the h_1var constraints. May generalize.
key_insights.depth_1_gap_confirmed: The depth-1 gap is real: exist_transfer from depth-(d+1) agreement gives depth-d existential, but quantifier conditions need depth-(d+1) existential. The IH bridges one level per application. The full chain recurses to d=0 where the gap materializes as the base case problem.
